comment: This is a good set of 4 assessment questions. But the current-state assessment should go beyond applications, infrastructure, standards and governance documents (i.e. desk review). A socio-technical baseline must examine actual work: informal workarounds, reporting burden, incentives, decision forums, support practices, data trust, power relationships, user capability and who is excluded. These factors often explain why technically functional systems are not used.

public.text: This is a good set of 4 assessment questions. But the current-state assessment should go beyond applications, infrastructure, standards and governance documents (i.e. desk review). A socio-technical baseline must examine actual work: informal workarounds, reporting burden, incentives, decision forums, support practices, data trust, power relationships, user capability and who is excluded. These factors often explain why technically functional systems are not used.
public.suggestedRevision: Add participatory work-practice and institutional assessment methods: observation/interviews, workflow and burden mapping, information-use assessment, stakeholder/power analysis, support-capacity mapping, equity and accessibility assessment, and identification of locally valued use cases and functioning installed-base elements to preserve.
